# Merge fixtures

Language-neutral JSON oracles for [archive protocol v3](../../../docs/archive-protocol-v3.md). Swift tests in `ios-app/Tests/LifeCoreTests/ArchiveMergeFixtureTests.swift` and the Kotlin tests read these files. Do not copy them into a platform-specific tree.

A file with no `kind`, or with `"kind": "merge"`, is a merge oracle. It has `base`, `local`, `remote`, and `expected` snapshots. `requireSymmetry` means swapping `local` and `remote` must produce the same `expected` snapshot. `expectedOrder` is the timeline order derived from `expected`, not a field stored in the snapshot. Tests compare parsed canonical JSON, not whitespace.

`note-only-record.json` keeps a newly added live record with zero media, an empty title, and a non-empty note when the other phone is unchanged, in both merge orders.

`"kind": "fail-closed"` has `base`, `local`, `remote`, and `requireSymmetry`. Both merge orders must fail. There is no `expected` snapshot. `"kind": "parse-error"` has `document`. Parsing that document must fail. `"kind": "purge"` has `now`, `published`, `snapshot`, and `expected`. `published` is the last synced base. Optional `stampAt` stamps the candidate before purge; without it only purge runs. A tombstone without an expired published deadline in the same deletion generation is kept. Those files are not part of the merge-oracle id set.

`tied-addition-stamps.json` fails closed when two media addition groups share one edit stamp and name different ids. Identical envelopes are kept; `own-commit-seen-as-remote.json` locks that. `non-integer-rejected.json` fails parse because `byteCount` is `1.0`. `conflict-marker-survives.json` keeps a conflict whose stamp is newer than the base. `conflict-added-same-stamp.json` adds a conflict under the base stamp. `conflict-resolved-one-side.json` resolves a conflict on one side. `link-later-stamp-wins.json`, `link-keep-unlinked-vs-relink.json`, `link-unlink-vs-item-delete.json`, and `legacy-omitted-link.json` are merge oracles. `purge-expired-item-drops-links.json` is a purge oracle whose trashed links are already `present: false` and whose tombstones are already in `published`. `purge-keeps-local-tombstone.json` keeps a tombstone that exists only in the pending snapshot. `link-dropped-when-item-absent.json` is a merge oracle: a link to an item the other side already purged is dropped. `unknown-link-and-stamp-keys.json`, `unknown-key-named-at.json`, and `known-field-omitted-deleted.json` are merge oracles. `media-one-side-keeps-conflict.json` is a merge oracle. Canonical encoder bytes live in `spec/fixtures/canonical/`, not in this directory.

None of these files encode COS object-version ordering. `clock-skew.json` orders field edits. The commit race is the COS object-already-exists error, specified in the protocol doc. `expired-purge-vs-old-base.json` and `expired-purge-vs-offline-restore.json` are symmetric: an expired tombstone omitted by one side is a purge, and a side that restored it keeps that restored record. Merge itself does not drop a tombstone by the clock. That omission is a separate pre-publish step.

The deletion-generation oracles cover offline restore followed by redelete (`redelete-keeps-new-generation`, `redelete-keeps-new-published-clock`), old-generation omission (`old-purge-keeps-new-generation`), null restore metadata (`restore-keeps-generation-on-null`), concurrent publish (`concurrent-new-generation-earliest`), metadata loss (`lost-deletion-generation`), schema rejection (`invalid-deletion-generation`), and generation-scoped purge (`purge-redelete-counts-from-new-publish`, `purge-old-generation-is-not-proof`, `purge-new-generation-boundary`). `parse-error` must run the protocol schema parser, not just JSON syntax parsing. Every auxiliary fixture must execute its declared operation; a catalog or shape check alone is not conformance evidence.
